parole.significato: A traditional Spanish unit of mass, equivalent to about 1.8 g.
parole.testo: From Spanish adarme (“¹⁄₁₆ Spanish ounce, peso”), from Andalusian Arabic الدرهم (ad-dárham), from Arabic دِرْهَم (dirham, “dirham”), from Middle Persian 𐭦𐭥𐭦𐭭 (drahm), from Ancient Greek δραχμή (drakhmḗ, “drachma”). Doublet of dram, drachma, diram, dirham, and dirhem.

parole.significato: The golden jackal; a smaller sort of jackal, sometimes domesticated.
parole.testo: From Spanish adive, from Andalusian Arabic, from Arabic الذِّئْب (aḏ-ḏiʔb). Doublet of dieb..

parole.significato: An unburnt brick dried in the sun.
parole.testo: From Spanish adobe, from Arabic اَلطُّوب (aṭ-ṭūb), from Sahidic Coptic ⲧⲱⲃⲉ (tōbe, “brick”), from Demotic Egyptian ⁠⁠ (tb, “brick”), from Egyptian Db-b-t:O39 (ḏbt, “brick, block, ingot”).

parole.significato: A sum of money paid as a reward to the bearer of good news.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish albricias, from Andalusian Arabic البُشْرَى (albúšra), from Arabic بُشْرَى (bušrā, “good news”).

parole.significato: In Mozarabic architecture, moulding which encloses the outward side of an arch.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish alfiz, from Andalusian Arabic الحِيْز (alḥíz), from Arabic حَيِّز (ḥayyiz).

parole.significato: A saddlebag.
parole.testo: From Spanish alforja, from Andalusian Arabic الخُرْج, from Arabic خُرْج (ḵurj, “saddlebag”).

parole.significato: In some Spanish-speaking countries, a junior-ranking officer in the military.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish alférez, from Andalusian Arabic, from Arabic فَارِس (fāris).

parole.significato: The carob, a leguminous tree of the Mediterranean region.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish algarroba, from Andalusian Arabic الخَرُّوبَة (al-ḵarrūba), from Arabic خَرُّوب (ḵarrūb, “carob”).

parole.significato: A lightly-clad footsoldier during the Christian reconquest of Islamic Spain.
parole.testo: From Spanish almogávar, from Andalusian Arabic المُغَاوِر (al-muḡā́wir), from Arabic مُغَاوِر (muḡāwir).

parole.significato: Synonym of espadrille.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish alpargata.

parole.significato: A form of grape concentrate, typically produced in Spain, made by boiling unfermented grape juice into a syrup. It may…
parole.testo: From Spanish, from Andalusian Arabic الرُّبّ (ar-rúbb), from Arabic رُبّ (rubb).

parole.significato: Any Spanish rice-based dish.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish arroz, from Old Spanish arroz, borrowed from Andalusian Arabic روز (rawz), from Arabic *رَوْز (*rawz), from رُزّ (ruzz), borrowed from Ancient Greek ὄρυζα (óruza), from Proto-Iranian *wrinǰiš, from *wriHǰíš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wriHǰʰíš. Doublet of rice. The initial vowel

parole.significato: A traditional unit of dry measure equivalent to about 665.8 L.
parole.testo: From Spanish cahíz, from Old Spanish cafiz, from Andalusian Arabic and Arabic قَفِيز (qafīz, “qafiz”), from Aramaic קְפִיזָא and Classical Syriac ܩܦܝܙܐ (qəp̄īzā), of uncertain derivation from Egyptian, Akkadian, and similar units. Doublet of qafiz and cafiso. Cognate with Ancient Greek καπίθη (kapít

parole.significato: A traditional Spanish unit of dry measure, equivalent to about 4.6 liters.
parole.testo: From Spanish celemín, from Andalusian Arabic, from Arabic ثُمُنِ (ṯumuni, “of one-eighth”). Doublet of tomin and azumbre.

parole.significato: A dish of fish (or sometimes chicken) first fried then marinated in a spiced vinegar and served cold.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from Spanish escabeche, from Andalusian Arabic اَلسُّكَّبَاج (assukkabáj), from Arabic اَلسِّكْبَاجَة (as-sikbāja), feminine of سِكْبَاج (sikbāj), from Middle Persian [script needed] (*sḵbʾk' /⁠*sikbāg⁠/) (whence Persian سکبا (sekbâ)). Possibly related to ceviche. Doublet of cave

parole.significato: A traditional Spanish unit of dry measure, chiefly used for grain and roughly equivalent to a bushel.
parole.testo: From Spanish fanega, from Andalusian Arabic فَنِيقَة (faníqa, “sack”), from Arabic فَنِيقَة (fanīqa).

parole.significato: A peccary (Tayassuidae spp.), especially a collared peccary (Dicotyles tajacu).
parole.testo: From Spanish javalina, jabalina, feminine form of jabalí (“wild boar”), from Andalusian Arabic جَبَلِي (jabalī) (in خِنْزِير جَبَلِيّ (ḵinzīr jabaliyy, “mountain pig”)), from Arabic جَبَل (jabal, “mountain”). Cognate with Portuguese javalina, and similar in other Iberian languages.

parole.significato: Synonym of medio, half-celemin, a traditional Spanish unit of dry measure equivalent to about 2.3 L.
parole.testo: From Spanish maquila, from Andalusian Arabic مَكِيلَة (makíla), from Arabic مَكِيلَة (makīla, “measured”). In reference to factories, via Spanish clipping of maquiladora, from maquilar (“to assemble”) + -adora (“-ator: forming agent nouns”), from maquilar's original sense of taking a toll of grain.

parole.significato: A mill for crushing ore, powered by horses or mules.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish tahona, from Old Spanish atahona, borrowed from Andalusian Arabic, from Arabic طَاحُونَة (ṭāḥūna).

parole.significato: A traditional Spanish unit of mass, equivalent to about 0.6 g.
parole.testo: From Spanish tomín, from Andalusian Arabic ثُمْن (ṯúmn), from Arabic ثُمْن (ṯumn, “one-eighth”), from the root ن (n) م (m) ث (ṯ-m-n). Originally used in reference to it forming one-eighth of a castellano.
